questions.prompt: The floor's job in a dispute is to…

choices.text: Apply the house rules to the facts.
Award the pot to the regular.
Poll the table and take a vote.

questions.explanation: The floor decides procedure. It is not a popularity contest.

questions.prompt: Your cards hit the muck by accident and are irretrievably mixed. Expect…

choices.text: A guaranteed refund of the pot.
A dead hand, unless the dealer can still clearly identify them.
A new deal of only your cards.

questions.explanation: Fouled or indistinguishable cards are usually dead. Protect them before that happens.

choices.text: It lets you see future cards.
Out-of-turn action changes what later players do and may bind you.
Only the big blind may speak.

questions.explanation: Order of action is part of the game, not a courtesy.

choices.text: Show me the cards you folded last hand.
Let me use your account to hold my chips.
Tell me what to bet; I will raise you back.
Dealer, please count the pot before I call.

questions.explanation: A pot count is normal. Fishing for folded cards, sharing accounts, or chip-dumping is not.
